title: Likes small things
text: “Good for you, I say.”
“……Should Ren perhaps interfere with Amaki-sama’s plans here?”
“Back off. And sit still while you get doted on.”
“Vof… Teo, leave guarding Naofumi-sama’s back to me.”
“Hold on, Shion, Wolf! Are you two abandoning me?! No matter what, I’ll make myself into something adorable and use it as a shield!”
And so, the Rabbit Guys began some sort of squabble amongst themselves.
“Somehow this keeps derailing further and further… I don’t think Ren needs to resist that hard, honestly…”
“……Did we pick the wrong one to rely on? Either way, there’s no turning back now. We will be away from this land for a while. The rest is up to you.”

Speaking thus, in an exchange I recalled having something similar happen before, Rival’s parent—a large-bodied monster—apparently finished instilling various things into what seemed to be Rival’s sibling, entrusted the rest to it, and settled into the egg.
“Even implanted the monster crest and everything.”
“It specifically named only Naofumi. Even though I offered to help too.”
“Well, I handled that part as the representative, so.”
“Fine by me. Taking responsibility isn’t my thing.”

According to Father, Ren has such a strong sense of responsibility that he doesn’t casually take things on—but once he decides something, he sees it through to the bitter end, indeed. Well, it seems that very sense of responsibility was what made Assistant from his original world wary of him. The egg began to shake, thump-thump.
“Come to think of it, didn’t it say its name was Gaelion… isn’t that the name Rafumi mentioned?”
“Still, there was something in the way it said it, like it implied this dragon was different somehow.”
“That one won’t say anything.”
“True enough… well, so we carry this over to Wyndia-chan, and as her sibling, watch over and protect it, is that the plan?”
“So taking the place of the adopted child’s sibling because it’s cute, playing baby games with it… what an advanced-level pervert.”
“Teo, you’d best keep quiet about that. Say something like that and you might get roasted later.”

I was in complete agreement with Rabbit Guy’s assessment, I say. It seemed the situation would end with only the parent residing inside Rival’s body. ……Come to think of it, I remembered how Rival had once compacted the parent that was inside its body. Even in this loop, it seemed likely that Rival would eventually return and meet a similar fate. Either way, vigilance was required. Father needed to graduate from bachelorhood before Rival came storming in, indeed. And yet, things simply weren’t going well. For now, he seemed to be getting along fine with Panda—I had indeed seen Father using Panda as a backrest, just as Rabbit Guy had instructed—so I decided to keep observing. But now that I thought of it, Older Sister also seemed to have used Father as a backrest, or been used as one by him… how exactly did that work out, I wondered?
“Vof, dragon… caution needed. Naofumi-sama, be careful.”
“I know, I know. But it seemed more like a worried father over Wyndia-chan, so it should be fine.”
“Higher dragons, regardless of sex, can be made to bear children. That trait… my own… no, never mind. Vof—.”
Wolf started to say something but cut himself off partway through. What were you about to say, hm? Somehow, my sensors seemed to have let out a faint warning beep.
“So what hatches will be a baby dragon, then.”
“I wonder if Luna gets clingy when baby dragons are cute?”
“She doesn’t, I say.”
Even in its baby dragon form, Rival got absolutely no reaction out of her. Well, I won’t deny that thing has an unsettling appearance regardless.
“So her strike zone is Keel-san and Amaki-sama, is it?”
“Most troublesome indeed. You two should just qualify as ‘cute’ as well!”
“By the way, just a hunch, but I think Teo’s within the ‘cute’ range, though probably not the size Luna-chan prefers, so maybe second or third string?”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah. Luna-chan’s big herself, so she likes small ones. So even though Teo became a big rabbit beastman and counts as cute, I think he’s still ranked low.”
“I see, what a relief.”
“What’s there to be relieved about. Try understanding the feelings of the one being inconvenienced here.”

Ren continued muttering as he made his way down the mountain, indeed. Quite right. Luna-chan preferred small, cute things. If anything, I suspected Father was the one who liked the big ones. Either way, I had to make sure not to get too close to Rival’s egg or the parent residing within it, indeed. Otherwise, who knew when Rival might take up residence again. And so, thinking such thoughts, we made our way back to the circus tent, I say.
The next morning, indeed.
“Ah, she’s awake. She’s awake, Shield Hero-sama.”

Mole, who had been watching over Assistant—who’d cried herself to sleep—called out to Father as she noticed her waking up. Naturally, Rival’s egg had been placed right by Assistant’s pillow. Keel and Ren were also sleeping there together. Luna-chan had been eyeing Rival’s egg with distaste, but she stayed quiet, sleeping beside Keel and Ren.
“Here… is…ah…”
Recalling what had happened before she fell asleep, Assistant’s face crumpled as if she might cry, then her gaze shifted to the egg looming large by her pillow.
“Morning, Wyndia-chan.”
Just as before, Assistant shot Father a somewhat displeased look before turning her gaze back to the egg.
“Your father exiled you, but he still came to leave your belongings with me. Including that egg.”
“But this egg… it wasn’t hatching… huh?”
Touching the egg and feeling its heartbeat, Assistant tilted her head in confusion.
“What’s wrong?”
“This egg never hatched at all, but now I can hear a heartbeat.”

“Is that so. Good to hear. Let’s properly introduce ourselves again, shall we? My name is Naofumi Iwatani. I’m the owner of this circus. And Keel-kun and the others who chased after you to help are kids I’m taking care of.”

Father, it seemed, intended to keep his identity as a Hero hidden while planning to bring Assistant along to Panda’s village. The plan seemed to be to let her live peacefully in the village, gradually level up enough to protect herself, and receive the same kind of education as Keel and the others.
Assistant turned her gaze to Keel, who had lain down beside her out of worry after she’d cried herself to sleep.
“Um… that…”
Mole, having heard about Assistant’s circumstances, seemed to be trying to say something too.
“Everyone here is good people, so it’s okay, really. I lost my mom and dad too… but everyone here took me in, and they’re all so kind.”

Father gently patted Mole’s head as she said this. Mole narrowed her eyes contentedly at the touch. Mole’s relatives were still in the process of being tracked down to confirm her identity. We knew she’d eventually be taken to Zeltoble, but the notice hadn’t arrived yet.

“Do you know this one? Imiya-chan. Her real name’s actually really long, though. And the ones sleeping there are Keel-kun, Ren, and Luna-chan. The one watching us from a bit further away is Motoyasu-kun.”
Father was introducing everyone present to Assistant.
“My name is… Wyndia.”
Once she’d finished introducing herself, Assistant turned her attention back to the egg.
“I can hear the heartbeat. It seems like it’ll hatch soon. But… I can tell it won’t hatch unless something is done.”
“Sounds like we need to register the monster crest.”
“Yes, seems that way. There’s a response—it’s reacting to you too. If you and I both register, it should be able to hatch.”
Having answered, Assistant cradled the egg protectively in her arms.
“Papa… I was a bad girl, so…”
“Uhh……”
Father seemed at a loss for how to console her. In a similar situation before, he’d found a foothold for conversation by explaining that there was a way back to Rival’s parent.
“Wyndia-chan, didn’t you have some idea already? Your papa didn’t want to keep you in the dragon world forever, you know.”
“So that papa of yours isn’t angry at all, okay? We didn’t mean to kill him either, it’s just… well, we ended up being a bit too strong, that’s all.”
“I bullied Papa…”
“Er, um……”
Father gave an awkward, troubled smile.
“We held back so we wouldn’t kill him, you know? Really, we did.”
“……Papa said dragons are strong, but he’s also the weakest Dragon Emperor, so he never knew when his time might come. Once I realized Papa wasn’t all that strong, I got worried…”
“Ahaha, well… guess we showed you an uncool side of things, huh.”
At that, Assistant hung her head sadly.
“Exile… kicked out of the territory, forced to leave the nest.”
“Well… yeah. I guess that’s how it turned out. Do you remember what we talked about before you fell asleep?”
At Father’s question, Assistant nodded. It was the talk about taking care of her if she had nowhere else to go.
“We’ll help out as much as we can. Since we might have gone and done something we shouldn’t have…”
